newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lehman sees HK residential property prices rising.
newsitem.headline: Lehman sees HK residential property prices rising.

text.p: The trend toward higher prices in Hong Kong's residential property market is well supported and has further to go, Lehman Brothers said on Thursday.
Property prices should rise 11 percent on an annual basis in the period from mid-1996 to mid-1997, Lehman Brothers chief economist Miron Mushkat said.

The forecast is based on a study of macroeconomic factors that affect property prices, rather than microecomic proxies such as household formations on the demand side and developers' real interest rates on the supply side.

Lehman found that three macro variables are particularly relevant in assessing the residential property market outlook. They are real gross domestic product per employee, the price/earnings ratio of local stocks and the terms of trade.

"An acceleration in the growth rate of real GDP per employee to around 3.5 percent, coupled with a stable price/earnings ratio and steady terms of trade, will lift real residential property prices by 11 percent on an annual basis," Lehman Brothers said in a report.

"However, to embrace this as a working proposition for late 1997 and beyond is a risky venture, for the assumptions with respect to the price/earnings ratio and the terms of trade are unlikely to hold that far out," the report warned.
